findings.title: Catch block increments retryCount for non-SMS errors
findings.body: The catch block added in this PR wraps the entire try block, so it catches errors from `prisma.profile.findFirst` (line 111), `getBookerBaseUrl` (line 119), and `customTemplate` (line 138) — none of which are SMS scheduling attempts. If any of these fail (e.g., a transient DB connection issue when looking up the organizer profile), `retryCount` is incremented even though `twilio.scheduleSMS` was never called. After two such unrelated failures, the reminder will be permanently deleted by the `deleteMany` at line 29, losing a perfectly valid SMS reminder that should have been scheduled. The retry-counting logic should only fire when the actual SMS scheduling attempt fails.

findings.title: deleteMany cleanup is not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` added to the `deleteMany` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the original condition it was combined with. The cron job at `scheduleSMSReminders.ts` is specifically the SMS-scheduling cron, but it now deletes any `WorkflowReminder` row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. Today only this file increments `retryCount`, so nothing breaks yet, but this couples the SMS cron to a global invariant and will silently delete non-SMS reminders the moment any other code path starts writing to `retryCount`. The `OR` branch should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or the responsibility split should be revisited).

findings.title: Retry-count logic has no test coverage
findings.body: The PR introduces non-trivial new behavior: incrementing `retryCount` on scheduling failure (both the `else` branch at line 179 and the `catch` branch at line 190), and using `retryCount > 1` to delete reminders. This is the only mechanism that prevents the SMS scheduler from infinitely retrying bad numbers, so it is reliability-critical. There are no tests added or modified for `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`. The behavior should be covered by tests: e.g., a failing `twilio.scheduleSMS` increments `retryCount`, a second failure leads to deletion on the next run, and a successful scheduling does not touch `retryCount`.

findings.title: retryCount update is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: Both new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls (line 184 in the `else` branch and line 195 in the `catch`) compute `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value that was loaded at the start of the loop iteration. If two instances of this cron run concurrently (e.g., a manual trigger overlapping a scheduled run, or two pods picking up the same scheduled task), both can read the same `retryCount` value and both write `value + 1`, causing one increment to be lost. The reminder would then survive one extra cron run before being deleted. This is a minor concurrency hazard under the current deployment model but should use an atomic increment (e.g., `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })`) to be safe.
